Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

suspect noun and adjective

a person suspected

also the suspect, suspects, suspected, under suspicion, prime suspect

classical

Ter. Hec. 4.2.1: tibi mē esse suspectam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 1.17: meīs cīvibus suspectus
Traupman 197, 388

suspectus, suspecta, suspectum

suspected; as a noun, a suspect

The person who suspects is in the dative (suspectus rēgī, Sall. Jug. 70.1); the crime in the genitive (suspectus sceleris, Curt.) or with in (in morte mātris, Suet. Vit. 14). Suspectum habēre aliquem, to suspect someone (Plaut. Bacch.). Traupman uses suspectus, suspectī m. as a noun, “a suspect”.

Other words

  • is in quem suspīciō cadit — the person suspicion falls on

    phrase: a relative clause with suspīciō, suspīciōnis f. · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.10.3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. suspīciō)

Examples

  • nōn clam mē est, tibi mē esse suspectam

    I am well aware that you suspect meTer. Hec. 4.2.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • Bomilcar suspectus rēgī et ipse eum suspiciēns

    Bomilcar, suspected by the king and suspecting him in turnSall. Jug. 70.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also suspect, criminal, crime, arrest, investigate.

SourcesLewis & Short: suspicio · Lewis & Short: suspectus
